findings.title: Per-file policy caps count lines, so a capped rule file grows in prose with its per-file budget check green
findings.claim: Appending ~150 tokens (600 bytes) of new prose to an existing line of each of 7 zero-headroom capped policy files produces 0 per-file budgets errors from policy_lint.mjs:checkBudgets in 7 of 7 cells, while the same bytes as 8 new lines are refused in 7 of 7.
findings.mechanism: checkBudgets compares r.lines (countLines) against files[<file>]; bytes are only summed into the five aggregate caps, each compared against cap+_band (500 tokens). Line-joining or reflowing therefore buys per-file prose growth bounded only by whatever aggregate band is left -- the silent per-file growth ratchet-budgets.md says the exact per-file comparison exists to prevent ('a band there would buy silent growth in every capped file at once').

evidence.unit: cells of 7 accepting +600 bytes with 0 per-file and 0 aggregate budgets errors
evidence.machine: B3 cloud container, 4 CPUs, 15 GiB, Linux; node v22.22.2; CPython 3.14.0rc2
evidence.contention_note: box shared with D0-s3 (compute-heavy) and three light seats; a count, contention-immune

perturbation.change: one line before `if (r.lines > cap) {` in checkBudgets: also push a budgets error when r.bytes exceeds the file's baseline bytes (the harness injects the map in a throwaway clone)

findings.metric_definition: Of N zero-line-headroom capped policy files, how many accept +600 bytes appended to an existing line with no budgets error from a default policy_lint run.
findings.phenomenon_property: Every per-file policy cap must bound the file's prose (bytes/tokens), not a quantity a reflow changes without changing the prose.
findings.seam_rule: grep -n 'r.lines > cap' .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs; python3 -c "import json;print(len(json.load(open('.claude/workflows/policy_budgets.json'))['files']))"  (every entry of files{} is a seam)

null_control.value: unmodified clone: 0 per-file budgets errors on the 7 cells, 0 aggregate; NEWLINES arm (same bytes, new lines): refused 7 of 7
null_control.note: the live control proves the per-file check is alive; only the unit is blind

reproduction_steps: run caps_unit.py from the export root
read the CELL lines: joined pf=0 agg=0, newlines pf=1
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Record per-file caps in bytes or tokens (or add a byte cap beside the line cap) in policy_budgets.json and compare them exactly in checkBudgets; ratchet-budgets.md's per-file paragraph then states the unit. Owner approval needed (policy).

findings.title: policy_lint --hooks never reads a hook's matcher: a PreToolUse matcher naming no edit tool passes as wired
findings.claim: With .claude/settings.json's PreToolUse matcher replaced by any of 4 values that match no file-editing tool (Read, Bash, Glob, NoSuchTool), policy_lint.mjs:cmdHooks exits 0 ('HOOKS ok: 3 wired hook(s)') in 4 of 4, although pre-edit.sh would then never run on an Edit/Write.
findings.mechanism: cmdHooks iterates event -> group -> hook, extracts the script path from the command and runs its --self-test; REQUIRED checks only (event, script) pairs. g.matcher is read nowhere, and pre-edit.sh's self-test drives decide() directly, so neither sees the matcher that decides whether Claude Code ever invokes the hook.

evidence.machine: B3 cloud container, 4 CPUs, 15 GiB, Linux; node v22.22.2; CPython 3.14.0rc2
evidence.contention_note: box shared with D0-s3 (compute-heavy) and three light seats; a count, contention-immune

perturbation.change: one line after `const script = ...` in cmdHooks: a PreToolUse group whose matcher regex does not match 'Edit' is pushed as NOT WIRED (applied in a throwaway clone)
perturbation.observed_value: variants refused 0 -> 4; tracked settings still rc 0

findings.metric_definition: Of 4 settings.json variants whose PreToolUse matcher matches no editing tool, how many make `policy_lint.mjs --hooks <file>` exit non-zero.
findings.phenomenon_property: The hook-wiring check must refuse any settings.json in which a required hook cannot fire on the tool events its rule targets -- event, script AND matcher.
findings.seam_rule: python3 -c "import json;s=json.load(open('.claude/settings.json'));print([(e,g.get('matcher')) for e,gs in s['hooks'].items() for g in gs])"

null_control.value: tracked settings rc=0; live control (script renamed to pre-edit-gone.sh) rc=1 'HOOKS REFUSED'
null_control.note: the check is alive for the script path; blind only to the matcher

reproduction_steps: or: copy .claude/settings.json, set PreToolUse[0].matcher to "Read", run node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --hooks <relative path to copy>
findings.proposed_fix_scope: cmdHooks: add the expected matcher to each REQUIRED row (PreToolUse must match Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit) and refuse otherwise; a fixture under fixtures/policy-rot/hooks/ with a wrong matcher pins it. The fix is in D11-s1's file; the defect is observed through my cell settings.json.

findings.title: The owner-approval predicate keys on the tvofi account, and 6 of 6 sampled owner approvals at head were seat-given
findings.claim: Over the 12 first-parent merges before the baseline, budget_raise_gate.approval() -- the in-tree predicate for CLAUDE.md's 'approval is the owner's approving GitHub review' -- counts an owner approval at the merged head on 6 PRs, and all 6 of those reviews state in their own body that the orchestrator seat gave them; 0 human owner approvals at head are distinguishable on GitHub's record.
findings.mechanism: approval() and main-protect's code-owner rule accept any review by login tvofi / id 70032254 / type User. Under the owner's 12-hour delegation (quoted only in review bodies; no in-tree decision records it -- git grep -il mandate finds none newer than decision 0009) the orchestrator posts reviews with the owner's credentials, so the human-oversight point CLAUDE.md and decision 0013 describe is indistinguishable from a seat's review. NIST AI 600-1/AI RMF GOVERN (accountability, human oversight provable from records) is the bar missed; the delegation itself was the owner's choice.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md rule 1 quotes a mode line the gate does not print, and says FULL prints a zero it does not
findings.claim: Of CLAUDE.md rule 1's two claims about the gate's mode line -- the literal `MODE: SCOPED — 0 script(s) run` and 'MODE: FULL ... prints zero' -- 0 of 2 hold on tests/closure.py:print_plan's output ('MODE: SCOPED -- 0 script(s) run, ...'; 'MODE: FULL -- every test script runs, nothing is scoped out.').
findings.mechanism: print_plan writes ASCII `--`, CLAUDE.md quotes an em dash; the FULL line carries no count. A seat grepping a log for the quoted literal finds nothing; policy_lint's citations class resolves symbols and paths, not quoted output strings.

perturbation.change: print_plan's scoped f-string `MODE: SCOPED -- {len` -> `MODE: SCOPED — {len` (in memory, recompiled from its own source)

findings.metric_definition: Count of CLAUDE.md rule 1's two mode-line claims that are true of print_plan's output for a 0-run scoped plan and a full plan.
findings.phenomenon_property: An output string the policy quotes for a seat to key on must be a substring of what the producing code prints.

null_control.value: the MODE: FULL substring itself is present in print_plan's full output (the line exists; only its claimed zero does not)
null_control.note: separates a missing line from a mis-quoted one

findings.proposed_fix_scope: Quote the printed literal (`MODE: SCOPED -- 0 script(s) run`) and drop 'both print zero' from CLAUDE.md rule 1 (policy edit, owner approval).
